candidate.answerReason: The product is odd exactly when both dice are odd, accounting for nine of 36 outcomes. The remaining 27 give an even product, so the probability is 3/4.

methods.label: Subtract the odd-product outcomes
methods.explanation: Among the 36 equally likely outcomes, an odd product requires both numbers to be odd, giving \(3\times3=9\) outcomes. Therefore, there are 27 outcomes with an even product, and the probability is \(27/36=3/4\).
methods.levelReason: Subtracting the unwanted outcomes uses elementary counting within Grade 9 probability, without formal probability multiplication rules.

methods.label: Count even products directly
methods.explanation:
A product is even exactly when at least one die is even. Label the dice first and second; each has three even faces and three odd faces. An even first die can be paired with any second-die face, giving \(3\times6=18\) outcomes. An odd first die must be paired with an even second die, giving \(3\times3=9\) outcomes. These cases cover every even product and cannot overlap because the first die has different parity in the two cases. Among \(6\times6=36\) equally likely outcomes, the probability is
\[
\frac{18+9}{36}=\frac34.
\]
methods.levelReason: This alternative uses elementary disjoint case counting and the same Grade 9 probability model as the main method.
